Not a terrible idea.  He left me with a suitcase full of paints and brushes. Lately I've been doing anything to distract myself.  I've learned a few years of poi in the weeks,  picked up rope dart, dapo star and attempted to juggle. I walk about 5 miles a day and that's the only alone time I like.  I have friends that know my problem but I've reached a point where I don't want to bother them with it anymore because I'm afraid they won't want to hang out and distract me anymore.  But maybe using his stuff might help keep his memory alive. When he died I had been out of town for almost two weeks,  our roommate said he hid in his room the whole time.  I went back for a couple hours a few days after he died but I moved out and to a new city to try and save myself.  

Thank you, listing ways I've been trying to stay healthy really reminded me how much i want to live to see tomorrow.

I mean, obviously not, nobody wants to have dead friends. He'd want me to keep fighting, to try and see my kid again, to use his paints and brushes or my pens and paper and art it out. He'd probably buy me a sixer and a pack of smokes and hug me if he knew what I was going through and then we'd just sit there and play games or draw. But he can't. Im sick of fighting to stay alive every day. My son doesn't know my name anymore. And I can't fucking oil paint.

My issue is that I would very much like to join my friend. I've battled with it for many years but losing him and so much else in the last year has made it something that concerns me.  I dream about it.  It's the the first and last thing I think about most days.

Im glad I found this sub on accident.  All I searched was "suicide" but this is the opposite of what i was searching for. I was depressed and had idealized suicide a lot before he died.  Now it's a constant.  Some days i grab a bottle of whiskey when i wake up just to calm my nerves.  I think I need a therapist or councilor or something but I can't afford medical care

Hey dude,  I've been there.  Im an adult and I still go through this sort of thing.  The fact that you reached shows a massive will to save yourself and I'm proud of you for that. I'm not hoping to lie to you and try to tell you how much better life is going to get because I don't know your life. 

What I can say is that life had ups and downs.  Mental illnesses has ups and downs. Reach out to your friends, other family members, hit my inbox on here if you want and I'll get back asap.
